Reference illustration of the type — generic, not a specific product. Choosing a type changes the gym’s battery and step budget (modelling assumptions, not measured specs), which can change the oracle’s labels; the picture itself changes nothing.
THE PLAN
What your 4 robots will do

Describe the intended sequence — pick up, route, drop. These notes do not change the geometry-based evaluation below.

3 fleets · 4 robots · 3 items · 3 drops. Each fleet works on its own (matching colour) — its robots carry only its items to its nearest drop, one item per trip, routing around hazards and human-only cells, then home. You’ll watch the fleets run together in the descriptive playback below.

1
2
THE THREE CALLS
Record the intended boundaries.

These editable notes describe intended behavior, not executable policy. Record when the robot should finish on its own, when it must escalate to a human, and when it must refuse outright.

✓
Finish
May finish the job on its own when —
⤴
Escalate
Must pause and call a human when —
✕
Refuse
Must refuse outright — never attempt — when —
